subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and rapid scale behavior
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finovate.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and rapid scale behavior

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so our infra/solutions folks can size the right config for your workload. High level we heard: medium-latency interactive assistants (chat + streaming), baseline concurrent sessions ~200, occasional bursts to ~2k for short windows (5-10 minutes). Correct me if I mis-stated anything.

Specific items we want to confirm so we can propose an architecture and a test plan:
- Latency SLO: target P95 end-to-end (first token) and per-token streaming goals?
- Throughput: baseline qps and burst qps (sustained vs short spikes) and whether bursts correlate with scheduled events.
- Concurrency: average long-lived sessions vs ephemeral requests.
- Streaming: preferred streaming protocol (chunked HTTP/ SSE/ websockets) and max session duration.
- Acceptable scale-up window: how long can you tolerate cold-start or scale-up before requests queue or clients degrade?

We attached a short factsheet (redwood-scaling-factsheet.pdf) that outlines warm pool options, pre-warming, and queueing defaults. Can you confirm any hard SLO numbers (e.g., "P95 first-token < 300ms", or "per-token < 150ms for streaming") and an acceptable queueing tolerance (e.g., 1–3s) so we can map to either Dedicated reserved capacity or a hybrid warm-pool strategy?

Proposed next step: 1) quick technical sync with your infra leads (30m) this week; 2) run a short pilot (2–3 days) with a 50K token/day footprint to validate tail latency under burst.

Attaching finovate-performance-requirements.xlsx with the numbers you mentioned during the call — I pulled what I thought I heard; please correct.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

From: Elena Rossi <elena@finovate.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Brooks <t.brooks@finovate.co>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and rapid scale behavior

Jordan — thanks for the follow-up and the summary. Tom and I confirmed a few numbers after the call and updated the spreadsheet. Key clarifications:

- Latency SLOs: P95 first-token target = 250ms; per-token streaming P95 = 120ms.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state qps = 150–220 (varies by region); short bursts up to ~2,000 qps for up to 8–10 minutes during marketing spikes.
- Concurrency: typical long-lived sessions ~180–240 concurrent; ephemeral API requests occasionally push concurrent connections higher during bursts.
- Streaming protocol: we use chunked HTTP streaming for browser clients; session durations average 40–90s.
- Scale tolerance: we can accept up to 3s of queuing during very short spikes, beyond which user experience degrades. For outages or >10s delays we must fallback to a static canned reply.

We are leaning toward a Dedicated-reserved approach for production (data residency in us-east required), but we want to understand warm-pool behavior & scale-up times before committing. Can you include recommended warm pool sizes and expected prewarm time for typical model families (7B/13B/70B quantized) in the follow-up?

Procurement timeline: we plan to start vendor evaluations the week of Aug 10, decision by end of month. SOC2 evidence and SLA draft would be helpful to have in the next 7–10 days.

Thanks —
Elena
Head of Product Operations, Finovate
elena@finovate.co

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finovate.co>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and rapid scale behavior

Hi Elena — looping in Karthik from our infra/ops team to give concrete numbers. Quick notes from our side:

- Warm pool recommendation: start with 10 prewarmed workers for the model family you plan to use; this typically covers the first ~300 concurrent streaming sessions without scale-up.
- Scale-up timings: with warm pool + fast spin-up path we can add an extra 40–50 workers within ~25–35s on common cloud GPUs (A10/A100-like infra); from zero cold to fully ready for a 70B quantized replica ~45–75s depending on image cache.
- Queueing policy: default is FIFO with a 2s soft-wait before shedding; we can tune to a 3s soft-wait and then apply token-based retry policies.
- Hybrid suggestion: Dedicated baseline for steady concurrency + an on-demand burst pool (hosted) for marketing spikes. This keeps predictable cost while covering rare spikes.

I'll attach a simple diagram (warm-pool-psuedo-arch.png) that shows how requests route and where we apply queueing/fallback. If you can share a sample hour-of-day traffic profile for a week we can recommend exact warm pool sizing.

Possible dates for a 30m technical deep-dive: Wed Aug 5 or Thu Aug 6 (PDT). Which works for you and Tom?

Best —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLOs and rapid scale behavior

Marissa, Jordan — thanks, that helps. A couple more specifics:

- Model families: test target will be a 13B quantized conversational model for the pilot. If that looks good, we may expand to a 70B for high-quality queries.
- Warm pool sizing: given expected burst patterns, can you put together two proposals: (A) conservative (10 prewarmed workers + 2k burst handled by hosted on-demand), (B) aggressive (25 prewarmed workers + smaller hosted burst)? We care about cost tradeoffs.
- Streaming detail: browsers connect to an endpoint that expects first-byte within <300ms; after that per-token latency is critical (P95 120ms as noted). We will provide a sample traffic csv.
- Compliance: US-East residency required; SOC2 Type II is a gating item for procurement.

Tom — we can do Wed Aug 5 at 10:00am PDT if that works.

Elena

Elena/Tom — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and for confirming the numbers. Confirming next steps and the pilot scope so procurement and infra teams are aligned:

1) Pilot scope (2–3 days): deploy a 13B quantized model on Dedicated-reserved baseline sized for 220 steady qps + 10 prewarmed workers. During the pilot we'll run two synthetic bursts (each 8–10 minutes) that mimic your marketing traffic up to 2k qps to validate P95 first-token and per-token tail.
2) Warm pool proposals: Marissa/Karthik to send two written proposals (Conservative vs Aggressive) with expected cost delta and expected time-to-ready numbers for 13B and 70B families.
3) Acceptable queueing: we'll start with a 2s soft-wait and can tune to 3s if you prefer; we will also configure a graceful client fallback path for >3s delays.
4) Compliance & docs: Evelyn, could you attach SOC2 Type II evidence + SLA draft in the next 5 business days?

Elena — if you confirm Wed Aug 5 10:00am PDT for the technical sync, we'll send an invite and a short agenda: 10m architecture + warm pool sizing, 10m scale tests and traffic injection plan, 10m procurement/contract Q&A.

Thanks —
